newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Cargo says back to profit in H1.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo says back to profit in H1.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG (LCAG) said it returned to profit in the first half of 1997 thanks to improved revenues, currency fluctuations and cost-cutting measures.
Dietrich Seidi, spokesman for Lufthansa's autonomous cargo subsidiary, confirmed a German media report that a profit had been made but said no precise figure could be disclosed until after August 26.
Lufthansa is due to announce overall group corporate half-year results on that date.
"The improvement was mostly due to the dollar exchange rate development, increased revenues and cost savings measures started last year which are now bearing fruit," he added.
Lufthansa Cargo transported 812,400 tonnes of freight January-June, a fall of 0.4 percent on the same period last year

LCAG made a loss of 48.2 million marks in the first half of 1996 due to falling yields and market over-capacity and ended 1996 with an overall loss of 59.8 million marks but aims to show a profit again in 1997. Lufthansa chairman Juergen Weber said on June 26 that the cargo unit was in profit over the first four months and could end the year back in the black.
